A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same telephone-game study despite the revised title. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete Appendices A-B are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original LLM transmission-chain simulations, text-property measurements, attractor estimates, and supplementary experiments in Section 4 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including model/task comparisons, robustness experiments, and attractor-validation analyses.

M1.justification: The transmission procedure, task prompts, four text-property measures, and regression-based attractor estimation remain unchanged in Sections 3.1-3.4 and Appendix A.

E1.justification: Both versions use scientific abstracts, news articles, and social-media comments for the same Rephrase, Take inspiration, and Continue tasks. Homogeneous and heterogeneous transmission scenarios are retained.

E2.justification: The same six LLMs participate in the main comparisons. Figure 5 retains the Llama3-70B and Mixtral-8x7B Base/Instruct comparisons, and Appendix B.2.4 retains the same homogeneous and mixed-model conditions.

E3.justification: Both retain 20 initial texts, 50 transmission steps, the same metrics and hashtag preprocessing, and unchanged temperature and fine-tuning comparisons. The 100-text and prompt-variation experimental settings also match.

E4.justification: Appendix B retains the same analyses of sample-size robustness, prompt paraphrasing, task constraints, heterogeneous chains, collapsing behavior, and attractor prediction. The temperature and fine-tuning analyses are also unchanged.

E5.justification: Both report five seeds, mean and standard-error trajectories, standard-deviation summaries for robustness checks, KS tests, and Bayesian 95% credible intervals. No uncertainty-reporting practice or run count changes.

E6.justification: The numerical intervals in Tables 2-12, text examples in Tables 1 and 13, and plotted findings remain unchanged. Inspection confirms that the edits to Figures 2 and 5 preserve the reported outcomes.

T1.justification: Section 3.4 retains the same linear recurrence, convergence condition |s| < 1, attractor position I/(1-s), and strength 1-s. The appendix mathematical and statistical formulations also match.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and Discussion retain the same claims about multi-turn evaluation gaps and attractor dynamics. The revised title foregrounds an evaluation purpose already explicitly claimed in v2.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning task freedom, temperature, fine-tuning, and attractor formation are unchanged. The limitations concerning linear chains and extensions to networks, heterogeneous populations, and human-LLM interactions are retained.

D1.justification: Appendix A and the Reproducibility Statement retain the same sampling instructions, prompts, hyperparameters, precision, hardware, computational costs, and reported code/data access information.

R1.justification: The Related Work section and bibliography match. Neither cited-work membership nor substantive positioning relative to cultural attraction theory, iterated learning, and prior LLM studies changes.

P1.justification: v3 retitles the paper around evaluating multi-turn LLMs, removes the short Methods overview, and expands the Section 3.1 heading to identify the experimental paradigm. It also adds conference headers and a funding acknowledgment; most prose and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 2 revises axis ticks, labels, and spacing, reducing repeated labels between task rows. Figure 5 enlarges and repositions legends. Conference headers and text reflow alter page layout, while figure/table membership and appendix displays remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: Figure 2 reduces axis-label clutter, and Figure 5 makes model and task legends substantially easier to read. These provide limited but concrete improvements in communicating the existing evidence. The methods, results, theoretical reasoning, and appendix analyses remain unchanged.
